title: Horizontal height-one primes in a complete normal power-series algebra
statement: Let $(C,\mathfrak n)$ be a commutative Noetherian normal local domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] complete for its maximal-ideal-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. For $d\ge0$ put $D=C[[T_1,\ldots,T_d]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. If $\mathfrak r\subset D$ is a height-one prime (a nonzero prime with no prime strictly between $(0)$ and $\mathfrak r$) and $\mathfrak r\not\subseteq\mathfrak nD$, then $\mathfrak r=(h)$ for some nonzero $h\in D$. No factoriality of $C$ or perfection of its residue field is assumed.

source.place: EGA IV4 proof of Theorem 21.14.1, second and third paragraphs: coordinate change, reduction to one variable, Weierstrass preparation, and monic polynomial factorization over the fraction field. Bourbaki Algebre commutative VII §3 no.7 Lemma 3 and no.8 Propositions 5-6, also WANTED. No Stacks tag asserts this horizontal-prime theorem. EGA IV4 is WANTED locally; read the online English translation.

proof.text: If $d=0$, then $D=C$ and every proper prime is contained in the maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$, so the horizontal hypothesis is impossible. For $d\geq1$, set $A=C[[T_1,\ldots,T_{d-1}]]$ and $t=T_d$. Regrouping coefficients identifies $D=A[[t]]$. Iterating the one-variable normal-domain lemma shows that $A$ is a Noetherian normal domain (start with $C$; at each of the $d-1$ steps the previous ring is Noetherian and normal). The local-ring lemma gives maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak nA+(T_1,\ldots,T_{d-1})$: the displayed ideal consists exactly of the series whose constant coefficient lies in $\mathfrak n$, by separating the constant term and partitioning positive monomials according to their first nonzero exponent. The completeness lemma with $J=\mathfrak n$ says $A$ is $\mathfrak m$-adically complete.

source.place: Theorem 21.14.1, proof, complete-case paragraph, passage to B′ and its maximal ideal; online English translation https://jcreinhold.github.io/ega/iv/34-ch4-21-divisors.html

proof.text: Choose $f\in\mathfrak r\setminus\mathfrak nD$. Since $C$ is Noetherian, $\mathfrak n$ is finitely generated; the coefficient-reduction kernel lemma therefore gives $\bar f\ne0$ in $(C/\mathfrak n)[[T_1,\ldots,T_d]]$. Apply the axis-coordinate-change lemma to obtain $\sigma$. Put $\mathfrak q=\sigma(\mathfrak r)$ and $g=\sigma(f)$. The induced bijection on ideals preserves inclusions, prime ideals, $(0)$ and nonzero ideals, so $\mathfrak q$ is again a height-one prime. The assertion $\overline{\sigma(f)}(0,\ldots,0,t)\ne0$ says exactly that $g$, viewed in $A[[t]]$, has nonzero image in $(A/\mathfrak m)[[t]]$.

source.place: Theorem 21.14.1, proof, coordinate-change reduction; coefficientwise reduction makes the hypotheses explicit; online English translation https://jcreinhold.github.io/ega/iv/34-ch4-21-divisors.html

proof.text: Apply Weierstrass preparation over the complete local ring $(A,\mathfrak m)$ to $g$: write $g=uF$ with $u$ a unit and $F\in A[t]$ monic and distinguished. Then $F=u^{-1}g\in\mathfrak q$. In particular $F\ne1$, since $\mathfrak q$ is proper.

source.place: Theorem 21.14.1, proof, one-variable paragraph, preparation of f_0; online English translation https://jcreinhold.github.io/ega/iv/34-ch4-21-divisors.html

proof.text: Apply the normal-domain monic-factorization lemma to $F$. It gives $F=\prod_{j=1}^s h_j$, with $h_j$ monic of positive degree, distinguished at $\mathfrak m$, and $A[t]/(h_j)$ a nonzero domain. Since $F\ne1$, the list is nonempty. Repeatedly applying primality to this product in $A[[t]]$ gives an index $j$ such that $h=h_j\in\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Theorem 21.14.1, proof, final paragraph, monic factors over the fraction field and integral closedness; online English translation https://jcreinhold.github.io/ega/iv/34-ch4-21-divisors.html

proof.text:

EGA IV4 21.14.1 is WANTED and not available locally; the online translation page cuts off at section 21.5, so I checked each step's mathematics directly. Mechanical finding: lem-per-weierstrass-preparation-complete-local and lem-per-distinguished-polynomial-quotient are status-mathlib pure algebra leaves (exact matches exists_isWeierstrassFactorization and IsDistinguishedAt.algEquivQuotient). They contain nothing from the forbidden Artin-Gabber route (no Qbar_l, duality, Gabber finiteness or stable reduction), are still in the DAG and are also cited by lem-per-weierstrass-henselian-cylinder. They are used only at steps 3 and 5, for preparation and the quotient isomorphism, so the finding is accepted. Maintainer note: keep these two leaves if the dropped-route cleanup prunes orphans; their blueprint.from is stale. Steps: d=0 case is vacuous. Step 1: A is a Noetherian normal domain, local with maximal ideal nA+(T), and complete (Lambda=C, J=n). Step 2: n is finitely generated, so the kernel lemma gives nonzero reduction of f; the axis reduction equals the reduction in (A/m)[[t]]; sigma preserves height one. Step 3: F=u^{-1}g lies in q, and F is not 1. Step 4: primality of q picks a factor h_j in q. Step 5: the quotient is a nonzero domain, so (0) < (h) <= q gives (h)=q, then pull back by sigma^{-1}. New nodes are true and not duplicates. Coordinate change: weights w_i > sum_{j>i} a_j w_j make the lex-least exponent a the unique minimal weight; d=1 is the identity; works over any ring. The coordinate step inside henselian-cylinder is bundled in that node's proof, not a citable node. Normal-domain factorization: K[T] monic irreducible factors lie in A[T] by 00H6(1) and normality; A[T]/(h) embeds in the field K[T]/(h); the local clause holds because the reductions of the factors multiply to T^n. Neither restates the item. This is a first split, not a re-split; the item proof is a short assembly of the cited nodes; the four tool_uses are accepted. No changes.
